title: Tenant synthetic workload design and validation playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended approach for designing, running, and validating tenant-level synthetic workloads during enterprise onboarding, cutover canaries, and QBR-driven stability assessments. It targets customer-success engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers who are responsible for validating that a tenant's production traffic profile will meet latency, cost, and fidelity targets on Redwood Inference.

Goals and success criteria

- Validate tenant SLA / SLO alignment before production cutover. Typical thresholds: P99 latency < 450ms (generation-only paths), error rate < 0.5% for 5m window, and no more than 15% token-cost uplift vs. forecast.
- Detect functional regressions introduced by model or infra changes (output fidelity checks).
- Identify capacity hotspots (KV cache miss ratios, batching inefficiencies, burst throttling).
- Produce artifact for QBR: run report, signal deltas, and remediation recommendations.

When to run

1. Pre-cutover validation: after tenant config and telemetry hooks are provisioned, before final DNS cutover.
2. Canary validation: during incremental traffic ramp (1% → 25% → 100%).
3. Quarterly stability review (QBR): scheduled synthetic runs that mimic seasonal peak patterns.

Synthetic workload taxonomy

- Deterministic replay (traffic replayer): replay of sanitized historical requests (best-fidelity for output regression checks).
- Probabilistic generator (template-based): parameterized prompt templates covering length, instruction complexity, and tool-calling patterns (best for stress and variety).
- Spike/burst test: short windows of extremely high RPS to exercise autoscaling and fairshare.
- Long-tail test: low-QPS wide-distribution of rare prompts to exercise model cache cold-starts and fallback routing.

Design principles

1. Safety-first: sanitize PII before replay; enforce privacy and retention rules.
2. Observability-driven: every synthetic request must carry tracing headers and a unique synthetic tag (tenant.synthetic_run_id).
3. Signal parity: ensure synthetic requests traverse the same ingress, auth, and routing layers as real traffic (no bypasses).
4. Incremental scope: start with smoke → functional → load → spike. Halt on safety or SLO failures.

Required telemetry & assertions

- Core telemetry (required): request_id, tenant_id, model_name, route, trace_id, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, kv_cache_hit (boolean), batch_size, response_status.
- SLO/Assertion matrix (examples):
  | Assertion | Threshold | Action on fail |
  |---|---:|---|
  | P95 end-to-end latency (route: /v1/generate) | < 220ms | Pause ramp, triage |
  | P99 token-latency generation | < 450ms | Escalate to runtime oncall |
  | KV cache hit ratio (common-prefixes) | >= 70% | Investigate cache keying / prefixing |
  | Token cost uplift | <= 15% vs forecast | Flag for finops review |
  | Model fidelity regression (BLEU/ROUGE or eval set drift) | delta <= 2% | Trigger model rollback plan |

Workload construction checklist

- Obtain tenant traffic profile: average RPS, peak RPS, typical prompt length, usage mix (single-shot, chat, embeddings).
- Prepare sanitized sample corpus (size: 1k–10k requests depending on test). Mask PII using redaction script.
- Create templates to increase/decrease prompt complexity. Examples: short-instruction (5–20 tokens), medium-context (50–250 tokens), long-context (250–4k tokens).
- Define time distribution: steady-state, daily-peak window(s), burst windows.
- Map templates to routing rules (hosted/dedicated/private / fallback variants).

Validation run procedure (step-by-step)

1. Pre-flight (owner: customer-success):
   - Confirm telemetry forwarding is active and dashboards ingest synthetic tags.
   - Ensure dedicated canaries are provisioned for isolation (if required).
   - Prepare stakeholder channel and incident paging list.
2. Smoke test (5m):
   - Run 50–100 requests across each route/model. Verify reachability, auth, and baseline latency.
   - Command example (template-based):
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
       -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TENANT_API_KEY}" \\
       -H "X-Synthetic-Run: tenant.synthetic_run_id=run-20260210-01" \\
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
       -d '{"model":"rwd-small-compat","input":"Summarize: The quarter...","max_tokens":64}'

3. Functional regression checks (30–60m):
   - Replay deterministic corpus against pinned model versions. Collect evaluation metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity) against golden outputs.
   - Run automated diff job to compute percent of responses flagged by heuristic safety checks.

4. Load ramp (1–3 hours):
   - Ramp per agreed plan: 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%. At each step, hold for 10–30 minutes and evaluate assertions.
   - Observe batching behavior: watch average batch_size and token-latency.

5. Spike test (15–30 minutes):
   - Generate multiple short bursts (10x baseline RPS) for 2–5 minutes each to validate autoscaling and fairshare.

6. Long-tail sweep (60–120 minutes):
   - Execute a wide variety of low-frequency prompts to assess cache cold-starts and fallback.

7. Post-run analysis and artifact generation:
   - Produce run report with graphs: latency percentiles, kv_cache_hit ratio over time, batch_size distribution, error traces, token cost per minute.
   - Attach diff-summary for functional regression and fidelity metrics.

Failure modes, common root causes, and mitigations

- High P99 token-latency:
  - Root causes: insufficient batching due to low aggregation window, oversized model variant, KV cache misses.
  - Mitigations: increase batching window for non-latency-critical routes, enable smaller quantized variant, tune cache keying.
- Elevated error rate during ramp:
  - Root causes: rate limits, quota enforcement, auth issues, misconfigured ingress ACL.
  - Mitigations: throttle client, raise quota with cust-success approval, verify tenant API key and IP allowlist.
- Token cost far above forecast:
  - Root causes: model switchover to larger size, repeated retries causing duplicate tokens, unexpected long-context prompts.
  - Mitigations: pin model version, add client-side deduplication and debounce, apply prompt-length caps at ingress.

Runbook snippets and tools

- Redactor (Python): simple sanitize example

  # sanitize.py
  import re
  def sanitize(text):
      text = re.sub(r"\\b\\d{12,16}\\b", "[REDACTED]", text)
      text = re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[REDACTED]", text)
      return text

- Sample synthetic run job (JSON payload for synthetic agent):
  {
    "tenant_id": "tenant-1234",
    "run_id": "run-2026-02-10-01",
    "pattern": "ramp",
    "templates": ["short-instruction","chat-context"],
    "duration_minutes": 180
  }

- Quick queries to validate telemetry (promql-like pseudo):
  - error_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\",status!~\"2..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[5m]))
  - kv_hit = sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[10m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{tenant_id=\"tenant-1234\",synthetic=\"true\"}[10m]))

Roles and ownership

- Customer Success (owner): coordinates the run, confirms corpus, communicates with customer stakeholders, compiles QBR artifact.
- SRE / Runtime (support): monitors infra during ramp, performs fast rollback, escalates to oncall if P99 or error thresholds breached.
- Solutions Engineering (support): validates fidelity thresholds and performs golden-output regression comparison.

Post-run artifacts and QBR inputs

1. Run report (required): PDF/HTML containing the timeline, key metric graphs, assertion outcomes, and remediation items.
2. Fidelity diff report: tabular list of requests with deviation scores and sample pairs (golden vs run).
3. Remediation backlog: prioritized list with owners and ETA.
4. Cost delta summary: projected monthly cost impact if current pattern persisted.

Appendix: sample acceptance gate checklist

- Gate A (Smoke): All routes reachable, auth validated, P95 latency < 250ms.
- Gate B (Functional): Regression delta < 2% on gold-set, safety flags < 0.2%.
- Gate C (Load): P99 latency < 450ms, error rate < 0.5%, kv_cache_hit >= 70%.
- Gate D (Cutover readiness): All previous gates passed for 2 consecutive runs, and run report approved by SRE and customer-success.
